rv.q: Largely, their resourcefulness elicits some real magic, as every found object – from a swim noodle to a bit of netting, from a cell phone flashlight to cast away pieces of mylar – are employed to launch Pericles on his journey.
While some purists will never accept any change to a Shakespearean play, this *Pericles* earns the standing ovation it received on opening night—and likely will every night it’s onstage.
Not so at Boston Court Pasadena, where imagination reigns supreme and the results are every bit as electrifying.

Working from Ellen McLaughlin’s modern verse translation, Starbuck boldly tackles multiple challenges in her current production at the Boston Court — a resourceful and clever staging that delights from start to finish.
Boston Court's Pericles offers several strong incentives for seeing it... Most importantly, this Pericles is a great deal of fun.
Despite a mighty and delightful ensemble cast, the Play On Shakespeare 's modern verse translation of William Shakespeare 's Pericles at Boston Court Pasadena is a bit of a head-scratcher.

cn.t: Boston Court's inventive staging and strong ensemble enliven Shakespeare's messy "Pericles," though the modern translation's fusion with Shakespearean language creates an uneven rhythm that divides critics on this fresh but flawed production.
